title: Horizon Full Tour
notes: Narration for the restructured product walkthrough, in the owner's order: subjects, electives and university requirements first, then messages, absence and sick leave, then every other section. 'text' is spoken; 'display' (when present) is what the subtitles show. 'holds' lists sentences followed by a 2 s narration-free hold.

segments.text: Horizon is one platform for school operations and student services, in Arabic and English.
This walkthrough explains each part of the platform in turn. It starts with subjects, electives and university requirements, then messages, absence and sick leave, and then every other section.

Choosing electives affects which university programmes stay open to a student, and Horizon connects the two. Staff set up next year's subjects. Students and parents choose them online. Every choice is checked against university entry requirements, and a counselor approves the plan.

Aisha Rahman, the school administrator, opens Subject registration and selects next year, twenty twenty seven to twenty twenty eight. Each grade has core subjects, which every student takes, and option blocks, from which each student chooses one course.
segments.display: Aisha Rahman, the school administrator, opens Subject registration and selects next year, 2027 to 2028. Each grade has core subjects, which every student takes, and option blocks, from which each student chooses one course.

segments.text: To add an elective, she selects Add subject, chooses the subject, sets it as an option in Block D, and links it to the matching course in the university catalog. Because the course is an AP course, the AP switch turns on, and students and parents will see an AP badge. She also sets Mathematics as a prerequisite, and saves.
Offerings can be changed at any time. She opens an existing course, changes the periods per week, and saves. The block and the prerequisites are changed in the same way.

For each course, she sees how many students have chosen it so far, and how many students' university targets need it. Once choices are in, Horizon places each student in a class, and opens a new section when one is full.
Adam Nasser, a Grade 9 student, opens My subjects. Course selection for next year is open until the twelfth of November, and he chooses one course in each block.
segments.display: Adam Nasser, a Grade 9 student, opens My subjects. Course selection for next year is open until 12 November, and he chooses one course in each block.

segments.text: Each option shows how many of his eight target programmes need it, and how many programmes worldwide it keeps open. In Block A, AP Physics 1 keeps ten more programmes open than regular Physics, because the University of Manchester accepts only the AP course.
segments.display: Each option shows how many of his 8 target programmes need it, and how many programmes worldwide it keeps open. In Block A, AP Physics 1 keeps 10 more programmes open than regular Physics, because the University of Manchester accepts only the AP course.

segments.text: Prerequisites are checked as he chooses: AP Physics 1 requires Mathematics, which he has met. When he selects AP Physics 1, the summary updates, and AP Computer Science A is no longer needed, because AP Physics 1 already meets Manchester's requirement for physics or computer science.

Horizon's university catalog covers three hundred and sixty six programmes at one hundred and sixteen universities in fifteen countries. For three hundred and eleven of these programmes, the entry requirements come from each university's official pages.
segments.display: Horizon's university catalog covers 366 programmes at 116 universities in 15 countries. For 311 of these programmes, the entry requirements come from each university's official pages.

segments.text: Adam's goal is to become an AI engineer, with the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada and the United Arab Emirates as target countries.

Horizon checked three hundred and eleven programmes at one hundred and eleven universities for him. One hundred and thirty eight programmes at fifty eight universities in fourteen countries are eligible or on track. Each programme has a clear status: eligible, on track, possibly eligible, needs review, or missing requirements.
segments.display: Horizon checked 311 programmes at 111 universities for him. 138 programmes at 58 universities in 14 countries are eligible or on track. Each programme has a clear status: eligible, on track, possibly eligible, needs review, or missing requirements.

segments.text: On a programme page, such as Computer Science at the University of Manchester, each requirement is quoted in the university's own words, with a link to the source and the date it was checked. Horizon checks each line against Adam's record and plan, and shows which are met, which are planned, and which are still open.

Where a programme requires a specific AP course, the requirement is marked AP required, and for students on other curricula the page shows the A Level and IB Higher Level requirements. Where a regular course is accepted, it is marked any level, or AP or a regular course.

The Subject levels panel brings this together across all eight targets. In mathematics, AP Calculus BC is needed by three of his eight targets. In sciences, a regular course is enough for all of them. Horizon only suggests courses that the school offers, such as AP Calculus BC in Grade 12.
segments.display: The Subject levels panel brings this together across all 8 targets. In mathematics, AP Calculus BC is needed by 3 of his 8 targets. In sciences, a regular course is enough for all of them. Horizon only suggests courses that the school offers, such as AP Calculus BC in Grade 12.

segments.text: Programmes can also be compared side by side, with each subject requirement lined up across the universities.
Rania Nasser, Adam's mother, sees the same subject choices from her own account, with the same guidance on what each option keeps open.
Everything is also available in Arabic, right to left. The subject levels for each university read the same way in Arabic.
When Adam is ready, he sends his Grade 9 to 12 course plan for approval. Sarah Ahmed, the school counselor, sees it in her list as waiting for approval.
Before deciding, she can try what-if changes without saving anything. Dropping AP Calculus BC, for example, shows the three programmes that would change.
segments.display: Before deciding, she can try what-if changes without saving anything. Dropping AP Calculus BC, for example, shows the 3 programmes that would change.

segments.text: She adds a note for Adam and approves the plan. The family then sees the approved plan and the counselor's note, in English or Arabic.
Messages about a request stay with the request. The people handling it see the whole conversation, and any message can be kept between staff, or made private.
Each request has its own conversation. Rania opens her school bus request, and new messages are marked, so she can see what has changed.
Every message has an audience: family and staff, staff only, or private to named people. Before sending, the composer shows exactly who will see the message.
Staff only messages are never shown to the family, and private messages are seen only by the people chosen.

The family is told about a new message in the app and by email, without the message text. Side by side, the family sees only family and staff messages, while staff see the whole thread. Messages never appear in search, dashboards or reports.
Absence reasons, including medical details, are visible only to the people who need them. Everyone else sees only that a student or teacher is away and excused.
Rania reports Adam's absence from her phone, chooses illness as the reason, and attaches the doctor's note. The reason and the note are marked private.
Only the family, the attendance office and the school nurse can see the reason and the note.
In Daniel Carter's register, Adam is shown as away and excused, without the reason. The principal also sees only that the absence is excused, and who reported it.

When a teacher reports sick leave, the reason is visible only to the staff who manage leave. Horizon finds a free teacher for each lesson and assigns the cover. The substitute sees that a colleague is away, with the lesson notes, and nothing more. The cover board flags any lesson still uncovered, and shares cover fairly across the term.
Services are the requests that families and staff make every day, such as letters, meetings and changes. Each request follows the school's own approval steps, with an owner and a deadline.
Rania opens Services on her phone, chooses Request a school document, selects an enrollment letter in English and Arabic, and submits.
Mona Al Awadhi, the registrar, finds the request in her approvals and approves it. Her decision is recorded with her name and the time.
Horizon issues the official letter on the school's letterhead, in English and Arabic. Rania is notified, and the letter is in her documents.
Every request has a reference number and shows each step as it happens. Requests past their deadline are flagged as overdue.

Twenty nine services are ready to use. The school decides who can request each one, and how quickly it should be handled. Administrators can adjust the forms and the approval steps without writing code.
segments.display: 29 services are ready to use. The school decides who can request each one, and how quickly it should be handled. Administrators can adjust the forms and the approval steps without writing code.

segments.text: In Grade 12, the course plan turns into university applications, tracked from shortlist to offer.
Each application has its own checklist. Deadlines become tasks and reminders.
When a student needs a recommendation letter, the request arrives on the teacher's task list with a due date.
The counselor sees every student on one board, and moves an application to the next stage by dragging its card. Each card shows the application route, the deadline and the checklist progress.

Students and parents register for university fairs and information sessions, and the event is added to their calendar. Younger students start with a ten minute career assessment. They then receive a career report in English and Arabic.
Counselling, wellbeing and safeguarding records are the most sensitive in a school, so they follow stricter rules.
When a teacher is concerned about a student, he refers them to the counselor in a few steps. The counselor opens the case with its full history.

Case notes are versioned: when a note is changed, the original is kept. The counselor books a meeting with the family from the case, and agrees an action plan that becomes tasks. The case list shows priorities and service level timers.

A teacher raises a safeguarding concern in a few steps. It goes directly to the designated safeguarding lead, Khalid Yousef, and to nobody else. The teacher who raised it sees only that it was received and is being handled.

Wellbeing and safeguarding cases never appear in search, dashboards or reports. Every view is written to the audit log. Parents are never notified automatically: informing a family is a recorded staff decision, with a reason.
Horizon also runs the academic day: the timetable, cover, grades, lesson planning, trips and exams.
The weekly timetable is generated without clashes. Every teacher, student and parent sees their own week. Cover lessons appear on the covering teacher's timetable.
Teachers enter marks in a gradebook that works like a spreadsheet, including pasting a column from Excel. Nothing reaches families until the teacher publishes.
Students and parents then see averages and trends. Term report cards are produced in English and Arabic.
Lesson plans are linked to curriculum standards, so the head of department can see what has been covered and what is missing.

Each trip comes with a consent letter. Parents give or decline consent on their phone. The trip leader follows a live consent board. Exam timetables are published as a PDF and added to family calendars. Staff see their invigilation duties.
Parents use Horizon on their phone, without installing anything from an app store.

Horizon installs to the home screen like an app. Updates arrive as push notifications. When the school enables it, they also arrive on WhatsApp. Notifications about sensitive matters show only a short line, and a link that requires sign in.
From the phone, a parent can approve a request. They can book a meeting with a teacher. They can pay fees through the school's own payment link.
Every page works in English. The same pages work in Arabic, right to left, and are designed for a phone screen.

The principal sees request volumes, resolution times and service levels, week by week. Sensitive cases are always excluded from these figures. Pilot measures show how many staff are active, and how many parents have joined. Leaders can also ask questions in plain words, and get answers from the school's own figures.
For inspections, the evidence pack gathers the records the school already keeps, for any period. It is produced as a PDF in English and Arabic.

For the UAE data protection law, requests to see or delete personal data are tracked with due dates. Everything held about one person can be exported in one step. Erasure shows a preview first, and asks for a typed confirmation.

A school can start using Horizon within days. After signing up, the school has a working setup with services, forms, letters, roles, bell times and the UAE calendar. The setup wizard adds the logo, colors and school year.
The import center brings in staff, students, families and classes from existing spreadsheets, and checks every row before anything is saved.
Staff are invited by email, and parents join with a school code. Every letter, form and message can be edited, in English and Arabic.
For a group of schools, the group dashboard compares every school side by side, and shares services and letters between them.

Each school's data is kept separate inside the database itself. Roles decide who sees what, and the principal can check exactly what any person can see, and why. The school can export all of its own data at any time.
Every sensitive action is recorded in an audit log that cannot be edited. AI can help with drafts and summaries, but on sensitive matters it only writes a draft, and a person always decides.
Horizon is one platform for school operations and student services, in Arabic and English. To arrange a demonstration for your school, contact Nexus AI Assurance.
